title: Conditions attached to the gift
text: Grant Larceny collapsed after the private toast and has died. Until the investigators finish their findings, preserve the service materials. His unsigned gift agreement would rename the museum, grant him acquisition vetoes, and require Artie's resignation. The related papers include a trust amendment, withheld invoices, disputed ownership files, and proposed cuts to education. These conditions were scheduled for announcement tonight.

title: Reference room incident notice
text: All gala guests were invited to the preparation walkthrough. The shared room and reference cupboard were open to visitors. After the walkthrough, the steward discovered the C-17 reference vial empty and secured the room. The vial and service materials have been preserved for comparison. The inventory discrepancy is being investigated. A missing reference material is not, by itself, a finding about the cause of death.
rows: Contents of the sole C-17 vial

title: The two service bells
text: The initial examination found C-17 inside Grant's coupe. The communal cordial and food controls were clear. Service account: The coupe arrived in blue factory film with a white crest across the closed seam. I guarded that package during paper deliveries. At the first bell, 6:40, I cut through the crest, unwrapped the coupe, and left it unattended on the service table. At the second bell, 6:44, I sealed a clear dome over it. I watched the intact seal until the 6:46 pour and watched the glass until Grant drank at 6:49. Nobody substituted a vessel. Guests delivered papers before and after the open period too.

title: One vial, one missing sample
text: The steward inspected the sole C-17 vial full and sealed when the preparation room opened at 6:20. It was empty at the 6:28 closure. The cupboard was accessible only during that walkthrough. Laboratory comparison identifies the distinctive C-17 batch in the material recovered from the coupe. The batch log records one sealed vial of this formulation prepared for tonight’s walkthrough. No other aliquot was issued. The room was locked after closure; nobody could obtain it later.

appendix.title: Preparation department / access plan
rows: Only guest route to the open shelves
Outside the fixed barrier; staff exchanges only
appendix.text: The west counter is in the corridor, separated from the preparation shelves by a fixed solid barrier. The staff return slot passes loan papers and support sleeves; it does not give guests access to the cupboard. Staff did not issue or pass C-17 through that slot. Guests entering the east visitor door could reach the open cupboard during the walkthrough. The source was unavailable before opening and after closure.

title: The poison was on the vessel
text: C-17 was present on the inner surface of Grant's private coupe, beneath the cordial line. The communal decanter, food, serving utensils, and poured cordial control were free of C-17. The coupe's guarded transport film excluded interior access before the first bell; the intact service dome and continuous watch excluded later contamination. The solution was deliberately applied directly inside the open coupe between the two bells, before the pour.

appendix.title: Packaging and receiving desk log
rows: Blue factory film / crest crosses sealed seam
appendix.text: The original transport film stayed sealed until the first bell. Its factory crest crossed the closed seam; the recovered film bears the cut made during unwrapping. The felt mat has a stitched crest and no sealed seam. The receiving clerk activated the raised RECEIVED seal at 6:45, after the second bell and dome seal. Earlier working carbons and red-pencil corrections have no raised impression. Originals were embossed individually on presentation; a carbon copy is not an embossed original.
